choices: Alignment: rows with a blank or non-positive close in any of HYG, IEF, QQQ are dropped before returns are taken, so a log return spans consecutive aligned days, not consecutive calendar days.
Index: t = 0 is the first aligned day; log returns exist from t = 1; S_t and M_t exist from t = 20.
Primary sample: every t at which S_t and F_t (q_(t+2)..q_(t+21)) both exist; M_t exists on the same set, so (a), (b) and (c) share one aligned sample of n days.

Circular shift: the rotated series is S shifted forward by k positions with wrap-around (numpy.roll(S, k)) against unrotated F, k = 250..n-250 inclusive; the count uses slope >= b with no tolerance; the rotated slope is OLS with intercept on the full n.
Halves: first half is the first floor(n/2) aligned observations, second half the remainder; OLS of F on S with intercept in each.

Horizons (d): F5_t = q_(t+2)..q_(t+6) and F10_t = q_(t+2)..q_(t+11), each regressed on S_t over its own maximal sample (every t where S_t and that forward sum exist), not restricted to the 20-day sample.
Newey-West: HAC covariance (X'X)^-1 Omega (X'X)^-1 with Omega = G0 + sum_{l=1..20} (1 - l/21)(G_l + G_l'), G_l = sum_t u_t u_(t-l) x_t x_(t-l)', no degrees-of-freedom or small-sample correction.
Reverse direction: Y_t = c_(t+2)..c_(t+21) (equal to S_(t+21)) regressed on M_t with intercept over every t where both exist; reported as b_reverse with Newey-West t (L = 20).
Information convention: F1_t = q_(t+1)..q_(t+20) on S_t over its own maximal sample (n + 1 days); shift p computed as in (a) with k = 250..n_info-250.
Contemporaneous correlation: Pearson correlation of c_t with q_t over every t >= 1.

Warning rule burn-in: the first 504 observations of the signal (S or M, which both start at t = 20) are burn-in; the first signal is taken at the 505th observation (t0 = 524). The percentiles at t use all signal values from the first observation up to and including t (burn-in included), numpy linear interpolation.

Warning rule states: start invested; if invested and signal_t <= 10th percentile_t, switch out; if out and signal_t > 50th percentile_t, switch in; otherwise hold. Signals are evaluated for t = t0..N-2.

Warning rule timing: a switch decided at the close of t executes at the close of t+1, so the new position first earns q_(t+2). The 10 bp cost is charged at the close of t+1 by multiplying that day's gross wealth by (1 - 0.001).
Evaluation window: return days d = t0+1..N-1 (wealth 1 at the close of t0); buy-and-hold uses QQQ simple returns over the same days, with no entry cost.
Annual return: prod(1 + r)^(252 / number of return days) - 1 on simple daily returns. Volatility (ann_vol): sample standard deviation (ddof = 1) of simple daily returns times sqrt(252).
Maximum drawdown: min over the path of W / running max(W) - 1, with W starting at 1 before the first return day; reported as a NEGATIVE fraction (e.g. -0.35).
Invested share: fraction of evaluation return days on which the position was QQQ.
Exits: number of in-to-out switches decided at t0..N-2 (all of which execute inside the window).

False alarms: an exit decided at t executes at the close of t+1; it is a false alarm if the QQQ close at t+21 exceeds the close at t+1. Exits whose t+21 lies beyond the sample are not evaluated and not counted (reported separately as exits_unevaluated).

Missed declines: QQQ drawdown episodes on the close path from t0 to N-1; an episode runs from a running peak until the close first regains that peak (or the sample ends); its trough is the minimum close in it; it qualifies if trough / peak - 1 <= -0.10. Missed if the rule held QQQ over the trough day's return (close of trough-1 to close of trough). n_declines reports the number of qualifying episodes.
Return given up while out: out_qqq_logret is the sum of QQQ log returns over return days on which the rule was out; rally_given_up is the sum of only the positive ones.
Verdict: PASS if (a)-(d) all hold; WEAK if (a) holds and any other fails; FAIL if (a) fails. Criterion (a) requires b > 0 and p_shift <= 0.025.
